questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly culture, nature and language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay to find information before arrival. We got information always quite late, but the information we then got was good and informative. The international office at ULisboa was helpful over mail if you needed, but with most things you just had to be patient.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The school organised a welcome week with activites where we got important information, as well as the opportunity to meet other exchangestudents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found mine through a facebook group, but most other exchangestudents found it through websites. It`s not that easy to find housing, and it can get quite expensive. One should also definitely be aware of scams.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The Ulisboa campus is not that central, but the public transport to campus is quite good, so there`s no problem living more central if you want.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I crossed off that I was interested in student housing before I arrived, but I never heard anything about it. Lots of other exchangestudents did the same, and they never heard anything either. There is other studenthousing available seperate from the uni like Xior student housing, which I was told was quite good, but also quite expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a fenix account where you follow all the steps, and then you have to fill out a learning agreement with your chosen courses that has to be approved by both your host institution and your sending institution. The different steps in the fenix portal is clear and well-structured, but it was a bit hard to understand where they communicate with you back if there`s any issues.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The available courses in english was available online, even though they were the ones from the year before. We got the available classes for the upcoming year later, and there was some differences. Therefore I couldn`t do some of the classes that I wanted to do as they were not on the list relevant to me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change two of my classes on my learning agreement as the classes was full.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early and be patient. It will work out in the end, they just work at a different speed down there:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general the level was a bit lower than at UCPH. Majority of my classes was quite easy, and there was not a lot of readings to do.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style resembled a bit more like high school were you have multible tests and presentations during the semester that all contribute to your overall grade. You also get graded on showing up to lectures and participation in class. We had handwritten exams, and more focus on remembering facts than academic practice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Analising of the dramatic text, C2 English in the world of the arts, C2 English Creative Writing, Philosophy of art, North American Cinema

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Philosophy of art and North American cinema were both very cool!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, groceries and public transport were all cheaper than I thought it would be

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a great sport facility, as well as multible clubs you could join. Most of the clubs were operating in portugese so it wasn`t so normal for exchangestudents to join, but it`s definitely doable.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting involved in all the erasmus events happening through organisations like ESN Lisboa and Erasmus Life Lisboa. Such an easy way to meet people, and they arrange events almost every day!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking advantage of the great weather and nature by going surfing or going for hikes. Lisboa is also a great city for cultural events, and there`s lots of concerts and cultural events to attend during the weekend. It`s also a great country to travel in, so I would definitely recommend going travelling in some of the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Sometimes a bit tricky when you don`t know the language, but not too bad.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Approach them in class and make the first move

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It a bit of an old fashioned and sometimes conservative culture, and sometimes the systems are a bit analog.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very open and warm culture, also very alive and lively.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient and don`t stress about the paperwork, it`s going to be okay. Attend the welcome week, that`s the best place to meet other exchangestudents when you first arrive! Also, enjoy it and make the most of it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend doing the portugese course offered by the school.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet all the amazing people and all the amazing places I got to see

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the cultural differences in the education system

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
